messages:
neha: Heads-up — we're seeing a customer-facing burst of 429s after the rate-cap change from last night. Raising an ops huddle to decide whether to pause the rollout. Logs show the spike aligns with the canary cohort (10%).

james: I saw the same in grafana. Canary host pool CPU is fine but token rejection jumped. Looks correlated to a handful of client_api_keys.

platform-oncall-bot: ALERT: 429 rate spike detected on /v1/generate (region-us-west). 1m avg 429s = 48 (baseline 2). Incident link: https://ops/redwood/inc/1929

elaine: Customer @Acme reported degraded UX — chat messages failing with 429, they also mentioned duplicated retries. They've paused their retries but still hit limits. Support ticket 9682-ACME attached.

mike: Can we get a quick repro curl for the failing path? Need to confirm headers and auth flow.

neha: Repro snippet from affected client (redacted api_key):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":50}'
```

Response: 429 body: `\{"error":\{"type":"rate_limit","message":"quota exhausted for key"\}}`

james: Not seeing auth errors, only 429s. Quick check — the new policy increased per-client burst window but decreased sustained qps. Some clients with spiky traffic exceed the new sustained bucket and get rejected despite short bursts.

mike: So the canary config is effectively narrower for sustained throughput. Do we have per-key usage history? If Acme did big short bursts earlier, they may have burned their allotment.

elaine: Support says Acme's usage pattern is chatty: lots of short messages per session with concurrent connections. They also have in-app retry with backoff that was not adjusted yet.

platform-oncall-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: rate-policy v4 deployed to canary (10% traffic) at 1929810000 by deploy-bot.

neha: Proposal: pause further rollout and flip canary back to v3 across the 10% cohort to stop user impact. Also ask Acme to throttle retries briefly.

james: Agreed. Before rollback, can we try a targeted mitigation: temporarily raise sustained_per_key qps for the canary from 3 -> 6 for 2 hours to see if that quiets 429s? Less disruptive than full rollback.

mike: That sounds fine but it needs a quick config patch and a controlled push. I can patch the policy and push to canary in ~10m, will annotate with the reason.

elaine: Support will inform Acme that we're adjusting limits and recommend they implement jitter and exponential backoff to avoid retry storms. I'll also offer a temporary quota uplift if needed.

neha: Action items: (1) mike to deploy quick sustained qps bump to canary (targeted) — ETA 10m; (2) james to monitor 1m/5m 429s and per-key traces; (3) elaine to tell Acme and ask for example session logs; (4) hold full rollout until metrics stable for 1h.

mike: Pushing patch now. Patch includes: `sustained_per_key_qps: 6` for canary policy v4. Command: `./policyctl apply --target canary --file canary-v4-temp-qps.yaml`

platform-oncall-bot: DEPLOY: patch applied to canary at 1929876600 by mike. Change id: chg-4489.

james: Early numbers — 1m 429s down from 48 -> 9, 5m trending down. Per-key traces for Acme show fewer rejects.

elaine: Acme acknowledges improvement. They're still seeing a couple of 429s when many clients hit concurrently, but it's acceptable for now.

neha: Good. Let's keep the canary uplifted and monitor for 60m. If stable, we can decide whether to modify the policy permanently (v4-alt) or revert to v3 and iterate on a new rollout with a different burst/sustained balance.

mike: Also note: billing showed a small spike in token usage from Acme after retries earlier — finance FYI if we do a temporary uplift.

james: For postmortem we should capture: canary traffic composition (client concurrency), policy diff (v3 vs v4 sustained vs burst), and detection delays. I can start a draft in the incidents channel.

elaine: Support will file the customer-facing summary and offer a credits/billing adjustment if their retries incurred costs during our policy instability.

neha: Thanks all. If 429s return or latency spikes alongside rejections, we roll back to v3 immediately and notify customers.

mike: Will keep a rollback command ready: `./policyctl rollback --policy rate-policy --to v3 --force --reason "canary 429 regressions"`

platform-oncall-bot: MONITOR: 429s at 1929876700 -> 5; sustained healthy.

james: Marking this thread for follow-up. I'll update the incident doc in 30m with current metrics.

elaine: Closing loop with Acme — thanks everyone. (emoji :thumbsup:)
